items.title: Dorothy Tait Interview, 1968-12-21
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] You see a boy like young Tom Sancton, who played at George's Wake... [INTERVIEWEE] And we might say here that, uh, Tom Sancton is from New Orleans, which is quite unusual.

ctx.x: Mixed, mixed feelings, Tom. Uh, I think it's such a specialized art form it can get away from you unless you hear it and play it as often as possible. I think the tendency, there is, in any band, there's a tendency for a band to disintegrate, less ensemble and more solo. Uh, all over the world, really largely through George, uh, and the recordings, uh, young bands are playing New Orleans style. How deeply rooted this is, I don't know. You see, it isn't this present generation. It isn't the men between 40 and 50…
And we might say here that, uh, Tom Sancton is from New Orleans, which is quite unusual.
That's right. New George, you heard him. Uh, what happens in another 20 years? I don't know.
